The best accuracy was achieved by Self-consistency N=5 with accuracy 0.531. The most token-efficient method was Direct /no_think, with approximately 0.00469 accuracy per generated token. Direct prompting was the cheapest baseline, using about 10.0 generated tokens per problem, but it gives the model little room to reason.

Comparing CoT /no_think and CoT /think, /think changed accuracy from 0.484 to 0.391, while average generated tokens changed from 213.6 to 512.0. Therefore, whether the extra reasoning budget was worth it depends on whether this accuracy gain was large enough to justify the higher token cost and latency.

Self-consistency reached accuracy 0.531, but it used about 973.5 tokens per problem because it samples five solutions. This usually increases latency substantially. Few-shot prompting reached accuracy 0.359; the single example may help by showing the desired reasoning and answer format, but it can also hurt when the example's structure distracts the model from a different type of problem.

One failure case came from Direct /no_think. The gold answer was 36, but the extracted prediction was 100. This is most likely an arithmetic or reasoning mistake unless the raw output shows that the correct answer was present but formatted ambiguously.
